The graph is small and very sparse (n=1418, avg_degree=2.61, max_degree=5, density=0.0037), which is the regime where neighbour-relative and per-dimension attribute views keep their resolution rather than collapsing to the global mean. The four selected views sit in four different reference frames: global per-dimension attribute space, neighbour-relative, community-relative, and attribute-space local density. (1) attribute_inflation is gated by exactly the conditions this graph meets (avg_degree=2.61 <= 5, num_nodes=1418 >= 500, feature_dim=21 <= 100): 21 low-dimensional attributes with only 25.3% zeros and feature_dup_rate=0.0 are continuous and count-like, not template rows, so 'simultaneously high across many dimensions' is a meaningful statement here and its degeneration condition (high-dimensional or non-count attributes) does not hold. Its landmarker is left-skewed (p50=0.689 above the mean), so the separation is sharper at the bottom than the top; I keep it first on mechanism grounds but treat the tail as the weaker part of the evidence. (2) homophily_violation is the cleanest neighbour-relative view available: its stated failure mode is large average degree, and at 2.61 neighbours per node the neighbour average is a genuine local reference rather than the global mean, while clustering_coeff=0.4832 means those neighbourhoods are coherent subgraphs. Its landmarker is smoothly graded with a real upper tail (p50=0.335, p90=0.691, p99=0.887), the shape expected when the mechanism is present. (3) community is well supported by structure: modularity=0.8814 is far above the ~0.3 weakness threshold and homophily=0.9524 says 95% of edges stay inside a Louvain community, so the partition is sharp; 35 communities over 1418 nodes is roughly 40 nodes each, small enough that a community centroid is not just the global mean, which is the stated degeneration case. Its landmarker is graded with a clear tail (p50=0.259 to p99=0.875). This gives a mid-scale reference between the one-hop and the global frames. (4) density adds the only pure attribute-space view: LOF degenerates on high-dimensional or binary-sparse attributes, and at feature_dim=21, feature_sparsity=0.253 and feature_dup_rate=0.0 neither applies, so nearest-neighbour distances do not concentrate. Its heavy-tailed landmarker (mean 0.103, p99=0.608 with the max far above) is the expected shape for a few genuinely isolated attribute rows, and because it reads no edges at all it is the least correlated evidence in the set. Rejected: local_affinity, whose landmarker is effectively binary (p50=p90=0.0, p95=p99=1.0), meaning about 6% of nodes are pinned at the maximum with no graded tail, consistent with the isolated-node convention rather than a measured signal, and it is in any case the same neighbour-relative frame as homophily_violation; attr_struct_mismatch, which has the widest spread (p99=0.964) but is built from homophily_violation plus an attribute-kNN ranking, so it is a derivative of two views already selected rather than independent evidence; spectral, whose landmarker is compressed near zero (mean 0.027, p90=0.065) and which can only see attribute magnitude, not direction; and reconstruction, contrastive, adversarial and one_class, which are trained views whose reference frames here are either neighbourhood-smoothed (redundant with homophily_violation) or a single global centre/discriminator, with nothing in the profile arguing they would add a distinct axis on a 1418-node graph.

The structure is unusually favourable to local reference frames: avg_degree is 2.61 with max_degree 5 and degree_std 1.43, so no neighbour-averaged view is at risk of the high-degree collapse toward the global mean, and is_power_law is false so no hub distorts the averages. modularity 0.8814 over num_communities 35 (about 40 nodes each) with homophily 0.9524 and clustering_coeff 0.4832 means the Louvain partition is sharp and its community centroids sit far from the global attribute mean, which is exactly the condition community needs; its landmarker confirms a graded signal with room in the tail (p50 0.2588, p90 0.6008, p99 0.8745) rather than a normalisation artifact. homophily_violation supplies the neighbour-relative frame at a finer scale than the community: 21 attributes, feature_sparsity only 0.2527 and feature_dup_rate 0.0 mean the raw neighbour average is an informative target, and its distribution is the best behaved of the fast views (mean 0.3843, smooth quantiles up to p99 0.8866). I take it in preference to local_affinity, which is described as rarely independent of it and whose landmarker is degenerate in shape: p50 and p90 both 0.0 with p95 and p99 pinned at 1.0, a saturated block of roughly 6 percent of nodes (consistent with the isolated-node maximum-score convention) over a mass at the minimum, giving no gradation to rank with. density adds the only frame that reads no edges at all, and its preconditions hold here rather than degenerating: feature_dim 21 is low, the attributes are not binary-sparse (sparsity 0.2527) and no row repeats (dup_rate 0.0), so 20-neighbour LOF distances do not concentrate, and its landmarker shows a genuinely separated minority (p50 0.0681, p90 0.2089, p99 0.6081). reconstruction closes the set with a learned multi-hop view whose two stated failure modes are both absent: neighbourhoods are tiny (avg_degree 2.61) so each node is not reconstructed from the same smoothed signal, and the attributes are not extreme-sparse so the decoder cannot win by fitting zeros. I leave out attr_struct_mismatch because it is built from the homophily-violation score and an attribute-space kNN ranking, both of which I am already running directly, so it would re-weight the same two signals rather than add a third. spectral is dropped on its own landmarker: mean 0.0269 with p50 0.0046 and p99 only 0.3191 is a near-constant scalar signal, and it can only see attribute magnitude. attribute_inflation is dropped despite being applicable because its shape is inverted for a detector, with the bulk high (mean 0.6416, p50 0.6892) and the tail compressed above p90 0.858, and with feature_sparsity 0.2527 and no duplicate rows there is little evidence these 21 attributes are count-like in the way the assumption requires. The four kept views span four distinct reference frames: community-relative, neighbour-relative on raw attributes, attribute-space only, and learned neighbourhood-smoothed.

The defining fact of this profile is that neighbourhoods are tiny: avg_degree 2.61 with max_degree 5 and density 0.003678. Every neighbour-relative paradigm here lists large neighbourhoods as its degeneracy condition, and this graph is as far from that condition as it can be, since a neighbour average is taken over at most five rows and therefore stays far from the global mean. reconstruction is chosen first because it sits in exactly that safe regime and is also safe on the attribute side (feature_sparsity 0.2527 is moderate, so the decoder cannot win by fitting zeros; feature_dup_rate 0.0 means no template rows to memorise), and it is the only trained nonlinear view selected, so its residuals are not a rewriting of a distance the other views already compute. community is chosen because modularity 0.8814 over 35 communities with homophily 0.9524 is the strongest number in the profile: roughly 40 nodes per community means a centroid that is genuinely local rather than a copy of the global mean, which is precisely the condition this paradigm needs, and its landmarker is smooth with a real upper tail (p50 0.2588, p95 0.7139, p99 0.8745). homophily_violation supplies the direct neighbour-relative reading on raw rows, with a well-formed spread (p50 0.3352 rising to p99 0.8866) and, unlike local_affinity, no isolated-node contamination since isolated nodes take the median. density is the fourth slot because it is the only selected view that never reads an edge, so its failures are uncorrelated with the other three; 21 dense dimensions is not the high-dimensional sparse-binary regime where LOF distances concentrate, and its landmarker does carry a tail (p50 0.0681, p95 0.3032, p99 0.6081). Deliberately rejected: local_affinity passes its gate but its landmarker is a Bernoulli flag (mean 0.0621, std 0.2413, p50 = p90 = 0.0, p95 = p99 = 1.0), so about 6 percent of nodes hold the maximum by the isolated-node convention while the other 94 percent tie at zero and are not ranked at all. spectral is collapsed (mean 0.0269, p50 0.0046) and can only see attribute magnitude. attr_struct_mismatch is the rank difference of homophily_violation and an attribute-kNN ranking, so its wide spread is mechanical rather than evidence of a mechanism, and both of its halves are already selected in raw, unmixed form. attribute_inflation sits high with a compressed tail (p50 0.6892, p95 0.8966, p99 0.9505), the shape of a saturated score rather than a separated set. one_class and adversarial are global-frame views with documented collapse and saturation failures, and a single global centre is the wrong reference frame on a graph partitioned this cleanly.

The four selected views sit in four different reference frames. linear_residual is first because its stated degeneracy condition is explicitly absent: feature_sparsity = 0.000357 and feature_dup_rate = 0.0002 mean the attributes are dense and non-templated, so the residual is not sparsity noise, and its landmarker has by far the sharpest separation in the set (p50 = 0.0007, p95 = 0.009, p99 = 0.8365), a small isolated group that no linear combination of the other rows plus Laplacian coherence explains. subgraph_contrast supplies the subgraph-relative frame and is the only validated port in the library; its density-based degeneracy is mitigated here because clustering_coeff = 0.4332, modularity = 0.5907 and homophily = 0.7791 keep a restart walk inside its own community rather than letting it reach an arbitrary part of the graph, and even the 5-epoch probe already shows a tail (p50 = 0.4069 to p99 = 0.7914). community is well founded on this partition: modularity 0.5907 is far above the ~0.3 floor and 12 communities over 8405 nodes average ~700 members each, so the centroids are genuinely local rather than proxies for the global mean, and the scores do spread (p50 = 0.0323 to p99 = 0.1703). density is included as the one view that reads no edges at all, maximising complementarity with the three graph-based views; its degeneracy case (binary or sparse attributes) does not hold on 400 dense, near-duplicate-free dimensions, and its landmarker is strongly tail-concentrated (p95 = 0.0143 against p99 = 0.0838). spectral is excluded because it sees only the attribute norm and, above 3000 nodes, reduces to the residual of one-hop smoothing, which at degree 48.54 removes almost everything; contrastive is excluded as the weaker fourth option since it scores robustness to attribute dropout rather than any node-versus-context comparison.

The dominant fact in this profile is avg_degree 48.54 with density 0.011551 and a compressed degree range (max_degree 87, degree_std 17.42, is_power_law false). That is precisely the condition under which every neighbour-relative view degenerates: the neighbour average converges to the global mean for all nodes.
